verdicts.note: Direction is well supported (no on the 2025 operating budget, 'reckless spending', tighter grant auditing) [S17][S19], but the dossier also records that she supports the superintendent's $2 billion school proposal if restricted to materials, supplies, operating costs and insurance [S16], and says schools are underfunded [S17]. That is accountability-conditioned new spending, not full restraint; -1 with high confidence.

Blames 'all of the green agenda' and the CCA for utility costs [S17] and voted against 2SHB 1409 [S10], but wants CCA revenue redirected rather than repealed [S17][S18]: -1 is the right magnitude, and a vote plus repeated statements supports high.

The basis mixes items that do not sit on the enforcement-vs-prevention axis: homelessness framed as drugs and mental illness and keeping newborns from drug-addicted parents [S17] are not enforcement positions, opposing firearm requirements [S19] is gun policy, and her overdose-mapping bill [S17] is a prevention/public-health tool. A lean toward pole_a is plausible but inferential; low confidence.
'I am in support of data centers'; 'I'm not so sure the state Legislature should do anything'; opposes a 'knee-jerk reaction to ban data centers' [S16]. Explicit, one interview: -2 medium stands.

Renter protections and down-payment relief [S6] point to pole_b, but in the same answer he proposes tiny homes and expanding city boundary lines so cities can grow [S6], which are supply-side measures. Mixed evidence with no detail; low confidence.

Platform: 'strong state-level protections that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement' [S3]; statement on 'unconstitutional attacks against our neighbors' [S1]; interview [S6]. Repeated and explicit.
